chapter.title: Chapter Three: Blue Side Blues
chapter.subtitle: Some doors are harder than districts.
chapter.description: Keep the Blue Side event open while Blue finally visits his father.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Who was that.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Your father.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* So you picked up.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He called the house. Twice Tuesday. Once yesterday. I just took the fourth one.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You've been having a conversation with my father in my house and I was at work.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He called the landline and let it go to voicemail, and then he called again, and then again. Nine times since Tuesday, Blue. Every single message is your name and then nothing. Then he stops.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: He stops.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He gets as far as your name and he stops. Nine times. I counted, and I'd like to apologize in advance for counting, because I know what that sounds like coming from your wife.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Wifey—

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I've been listening to a sixty-eight-year-old man try to say a sentence nine times. That's not a phone call, that's a man standing outside a door practicing what he's going to say when it opens.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He wants to tell you himself. That's what he keeps trying. He says it like a *plan*, like he's still got time to execute it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: And you're telling me because you couldn't be the one to break it.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I'm telling you because he called *me*. *(Beat.)*He didn't call Red. He didn't call Baby Momma. He's seen Baby Momma twice this month. He called the house and got voicemail, and he called me, and

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I picked up, and now I have it, and I can't put it down on a table the way you can.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Don't put it on a table.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Then what do you want me to do with it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What won't he say on a voicemail?

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He's sick.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: He's — what?

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He's still in treatment. He's been hiding it from you and he's not good and I have known since March.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: March. It's September. *March?*

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Yes.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: And you're — How long have you had that.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Six months.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *Six months.*

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I know what that looks like. I'm not — I didn't keep it to be cruel. I kept it because every time I thought about telling you, I thought about the week after, and I didn't want the week after.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: That's it. That's the whole reason. I'm not strong, Blue. I'm *tired*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You should've told me.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Yes.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Six months, Wifey.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *Yes*, and I have been waiting every single one of those months for you to say that exact sentence, because I knew you'd say it, and I knew I'd have to answer it, and I have had the answer ready

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: since March. *(Beat.)*And now I have to go and do this, and you're going to make it about how I did it instead of about him, and I want you to know I can see that happening right now.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Still holding the chairs.)*I got to ask — are we talking about your father, are we talking about the chairs, because I been holding these chairs through the entire family portion of this

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: conversation and my arms are about to become a *medical situation*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Get me somebody to run the rest of my tables.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(To the player.)*That is a *no* to the chairs and a *yes* to the tables. I want that on the record, because I been trying to get this man to hand over a clipboard for four years and I have just

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: been handed a *promotion*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I'm not canceling an event because my family can't use a phone.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Nobody asked you to! *(He finally puts the chairs down.)*Champ's right here. Finish your match, hand me the sheet, and go. I'll be here. I got nowhere to be, which is a *choice* I have made

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: repeatedly.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Fine. *(Beat.)* Fine. But not the house — I'm not doing this in the house.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He's at the house, Blue.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Then I'll stand on the step.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(She picks up the phone, and then she stops, and she looks at him.)*Blue. He's *sitting down* to say it. He didn't do nine voicemails because he was busy. If you make him stand on a step to do

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: it, he will put it down and tell you he's fine. That's what he does. That's what he did for four years.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: That's yours. I'm not taking a rematch on the way out of my own building.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Nobody offered.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You were building to it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Wifey. Was it bad.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: I don't know. He wouldn't say it on the phone. He said the thing about the voicemails and then he said "tell him I'm not rushing him," and then he said — *(Beat.)*— he said tell him he'll know

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: when it's the right time, because he'll know.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I'll know when it's the right time.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: That's what he said you'd say.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Calling across the room, cheerfully.)* BLUE! Blue, I got a question! Blue!

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: What.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Absolutely not a question.)* Dinner's at Auntie's on Sunday. You can be a person at it or you can be a *job* at it, and I need to know which so I can set a place.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I'll be there.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(To the player, immediately, under his breath.)* He said that. You heard him say that. I'm holding him to it, I got witnesses, and *you* are a witness, so if he doesn't show, you get to tell him.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Why me?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: 'Cause you don't lie, and I do, and I need at least one person in this building with a clean record.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I promised these people a match before I leave. You and me, champ. Cornball's on check-in and he's *thriving* and I need you to see what a functional operation looks like before it leaves.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: We could do this next week.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I've been doing everything next week for four years. You can wait ten minutes while I finish something I wanted to do.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Wifey, you don't have to—

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Don't be kind at me right now. I cannot handle you being kind at me right now, because if you're nice to me I will sit down. *(Beat.)* Shuffle.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Watching her take the lane.)* You keep giving me the outside.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: It's a good outside.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You keep giving it to me and then acting like you didn't.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I'm not going to be able to do that with you after tonight, is the thing. So maybe learn the lesson while it's still free.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Wifey.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I said shuffle.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Loud.)* BLUE! The phone's going again!

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Not turning.)* It's not my father.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Not turning either. Playing.)* It's the landlord.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: The landlord can wait.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Where'd she go?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: She said you knew where.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I said you tell me.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: She said "he knows where." *(Beat.)*And then she was gone. I tried to ask her something about the timer and she said "not tonight, Cornball," and I've known that woman four years and I have never

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: once heard her say not tonight.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: She didn't tell you where.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: She said "he knows where."

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: And you do.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I know where.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Closer than he should be.)* He knows where, and he was *on his way out* at the same time she was on her way out, and neither of them said the word.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Champ. You don't gotta answer that. I just want it said out loud one time in a building where *somebody* could hear it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Said.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*Good. *(He picks up a clipboard.)*Cornball's your last match here. After that, go by the house. Not because he asked you to — he's not going to ask you to, he don't ask anybody to do

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: anything, that's his whole thing. Go anyway.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Fourteen people promised, nine showed, and every single one of them let me win a round. *(He writes it down.)* That's my whole life on a clipboard.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(To the room.)*Blue checked that door lock three times. I timed it. Fourteen seconds between the third look and the time he pulled it shut, which is a long time if you're counting, and I been

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: counting all night, because somebody in this building has to.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I'm taking him over now. The match is the last thing. Finish here and meet us at the house.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Not looking up.)* You been crying.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: No.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Mm. *(Beat.)* Blue's the one to hold that in. You're the one to — *(He stops. Redoes it.)* — you and your sister got the same face right now, and I don't know what that is, and I'm not asking.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(At the door, quiet.)* Cornball. Why do you count.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Finally looks up.)* 'Cause somebody's gotta be the guy who noticed, and if it ain't me it's nobody, and then everybody gets to say nobody saw.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You're not playing your best.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I'm playing *fine*. There's a difference and it's about my wrists.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You're giving me rounds again.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I'm *setting you up for the seed*, which is a different industry, champ, and I got a whole *thing* about it. *(Beat.)*Middle district shuts in round three. Broken timer. I labeled it, so nobody

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: can say I ambushed anybody later. That's the last thing I got left to give this block and I'm giving it to you.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You keep giving people things and then acting like you didn't.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: ...Where'd you get that.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Wifey says it to her husband on a card table about forty minutes ago. You were on check-in.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(He laughs, and it's the wrong kind.)* Yeah. That sounds right. *(He sets the clipboard down.)* All right. I'm not gonna give you anything. You want it, come get it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Slowly.)* You took that one. *(Beat.)* You took the last two lanes and you didn't hand it back and you didn't even *look* like you were thinking about handing it back.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I'm playing this week.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Picking up the clipboard.)*Okay. Good. That's — okay. *(He's not smiling.)*Cornball's been the guy who gives it away since I got here and I'm not saying that's noble, I'm saying I *thought* it

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: was.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: It wasn't?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: It was *nice*. Nice is a thing you do so nobody can say you didn't come. *(Beat.)*You just took a lane off me and told me about it after. That's a whole different thing and I don't know what to do

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: with it yet.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Everybody got their turn, nothing caught fire, and I only lost one pen.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Lost it?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: It's behind my ear. *(Beat.)* Extremely well-run event.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Wifey's at the house.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Already walking.)* Yeah. And I got a clipboard and no reason to be at my own house right now, so.

tips: Continue the story at your own pace.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Dad. *(He stops two feet into the room, which is a thing he does every time.)*

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Sit down. Both of you.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I'm not sitting down.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Then stand. You always stood when we did this.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Not sitting either.)* Treatment. Since March.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: I knew since March. I didn't tell him.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: I know.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: I'm saying it to him.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: I know, and I'm letting you, and I'd like to say something about it and I want to say it after.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: So sit down and tell me. What's wrong with you, and what did you know, and how long.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: I'm going to tell you what's wrong with me. Then I'm going to tell you what I did, and I am going to get about a third of the way through it, and then I'm going to stop. I want you to hear that

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: from me now instead of being surprised by it in the middle.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Why would you stop.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Because you'll forgive me too fast.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: I've had four years to work out what I'm going to say to you, and what I've worked out is this. You have been angry with me since you were nineteen, and you've never once had a reason that would

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: hold up, and if I sit down with you today and hand you a clean explanation, you will take it. You'll take it because you're *relieved*, and you will call it forgiveness, and in about a year you

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: will be angry again and you will have nothing to hold on to.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: You want me angry.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: I want you *angry with the correct person*, which is not me. Not yet.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Who's the correct person.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Your brother. And he's not here.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: He's at home.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Then go get him.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I'm not going anywhere until you tell me what happened to him.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: *(Beat.)*I'm going to tell you he was doing a handoff, and that it went wrong, and that I found out before it went wronger. That's the short version and it's the true one. After that, it stops

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: being a fact and starts being *ours*, and I don't want to hand you a fact when you need a conversation.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Very quietly, to the player, not to the room.)* He's describing me. He just — he's *describing* me.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: I know.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: I've been sitting here for four minutes watching a man get it right, and I can't — *(She stops.)*

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: You're keeping something from him too. I saw it in March and I've said nothing because it isn't mine.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: It's not your business.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: No. *(Beat.)*But I want you to hear a man who's *just* been told he has to wait, tell you that waiting is a thing you can do for as long as you need, and then fail at it, and that failing at it is

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: allowed and it is the whole reason I am going to sit in this chair and let my son be angry at me for a few more weeks.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: The doctors won't give me a date and I have stopped asking, because the date isn't going to change what I owe you. I still can't sleep on my back. I get tired in a way I can't explain to anybody

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: who isn't tired. *(Beat.)*I'm not telling you that so you'll be careful with me. I'm telling you because I've hidden one thing and I'm finished hiding things, and the treatment is smaller than the

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: other one but it's mine and I want it out in the air.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: *(He sits.)* When did you know?

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: January. The letter came in January and I put it in the drawer with the tax papers and I took it out about nine times.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: I called you nine times.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I know.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Every one of them was your name and then nothing.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I know. *(Beat.)* I'm sorry, Dad.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Don't do that here, that's what we come here to stop.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: Blue, I need you to see something, and I need you to see it *now* before somebody else posts it.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I'm not looking at a phone in my father's house.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: It's not that. *(He turns the phone around.)* It's a video. It's four years old. And there's a guy standing outside a warehouse in a *winter coat*, saying your name.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Taking the phone. Looking at it. Then at Blue.)* Blue. That's your coat.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I don't have a coat like that.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: That's the one I fixed the sleeve on. Four years ago. You still owe me for it.
